newsitem.title: USA: Mobil, Conoco profits up despite lower oil, gas prices.
newsitem.headline: Mobil, Conoco profits up despite lower oil, gas prices.

text.p: Mobil and Conoco reported higher second-quarter profits Wednesday while Unocal, Chevron and USX-Marathon posted weaker profits as lower oil and natual gas prices affected all oil companies.
Mobil Corp. said its net income increased 10 percent to $850 million while Conoco said its profits jumped 39 percent to a record $246 million.
Unocal said its net income plunged by 50 percent to $118 million while Chevron Corp. said its profits slid 6 percent to $823 million and Marathon said its earnings dipped 5 percent to $118 million.
Mobil, based in Fairfax, Va., said its net income for the three months ended June 30 increased to $850 million, or $1.06 a share, from $783 million, or 98 cents a share.

The company said operating earnings rose 7 percent to $870 million, or $1.09 a share, from $814 million, or $1.02 a share. It said share amounts reflect the two-for-one stock split that took effect May 20.

Chairman Lucio A. Noto said the earnings improvement resulted from volume growth in all business sectors, strong operating performance at the company's U.S. refineries and improved results in its lubricants business.
These improvements were partly offset by increased refinery downtime in Asia-Pacific and somewhat higher expenses related to new business development, it added.
Mobil also said its net income was reduced by a $20 million special charge for start-up costs associated with its alliance with British Petroleum in Europe.
Chevron said its net income declined to $823 million, or $1.26 a share, from $872 million, or $1.34 a share.

It said the results were hurt by a $66 million charge related to the company's employee stock option programme while the year-earlier results were helped by a $172 million gain, mostly related to the sale of refinery interests in Japan.
The company also said, however, that its operating earnings jumped 20 percent to a record $837 million from $700 million, surpassing the record set in the first quarter of this year.
San Francisco-based Chevron said all its business units turned in strong performances, both financially and operationally.
Unocal said its net income fell to $118 million, or 48 cents a share, from $238 million, or 92 cents a share. It said profits were affected by a $38 million charge for the early payment of debt.
The company, which is based in El Segundo, Calif., said earnings from continuing operations fell to $156 million, or 63 cents a share, from $188 million, or 72 cents a share.
Unocal said its operating results were impacted by lower worldwide crude oil prices and lower domestic natural gas prices, and increased international exploration expenses.
Conoco, a subsidiary of chemical giant DuPont Co. of Wilmington, Del., said its net income for the three months ended June 30 jumped 39 percent to a record $246 million from $177 million.

The company said continued improvement in its refining and marketing operations, particularly in the United States, and higher international gas volumes contributed to its eighth consecutive quarterly earnings increase.
Conoco said sales for the quarter fell 2 percent to $4.9 billion as its average net realised crude oil price fell to $17.78 a barrel from $19.06 in 1996.

The company said its results included charges of $63 million for write-down of investment in a European natural gas marketing joint venture and $22 million for employee separation costs, whhich were partly offset by a net benefit of $44 million related to environmental insurance recoveries.
USX-Marathon Group, a subsidiary of Pittsburgh-based USX Corp., said its net income fell to $118 million, or 41 cents a share, from $124 million, or 43 cents a share.
It said profits were reduced by a $40 million aftertax charge for an inventory market valuation.
The company said revenues declined to $3.8 billion from $4.1 billion, reflecting lower production as well as lower oil and natural gas prices.

Mobil's stock slipped 44 cents to $75.06 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Chevron also gave up 44 cents to $77.19 on the NYSE while Unocal dipped 19 cents to $38.75, also on th Big Board.
USX-Marathon's stock added 25 cents to $30.50 on the New York exchange.
